h02.answer_text: Coca‑Cola (ticker KO) showed the fastest revenue growth in fiscal 2022 among the three companies, with a growth rate of about 11.3% (0.1125).  Its 2022 Form 10‑K attributes the revenue increase to several factors: a 5% rise in concentrate sales volume, favorable price, product and geographic mix, and a 11% overall increase after accounting for acquisitions and divestitures.  The company also highlights strategic investments in its brand portfolio, innovation pipeline, and data‑driven revenue‑growth management, which together supported the higher sales and pricing initiatives.  While foreign‑currency headwinds and higher commodity and marketing costs partially offset the gains, the net effect was an 11% rise in net operating revenues from $38.7 billion in 2021 to $43.0 billion in 2022.

h13.answer_text: The average revenue growth across all companies in fiscal 2022 was 0.1069 (about 10.7%).  AMD’s 2022 Form 10‑K explains that its revenue change was driven by several factors: higher semi‑custom product sales and a large increase in Embedded‑segment revenue from the inclusion of Xilinx‑derived embedded product sales after the February 2022 acquisition; a 10% decline in Client‑segment revenue caused by lower processor shipments tied to a weak PC market and inventory‑correction actions; and, in the Gaming segment, higher semi‑custom sales for console SoCs offset by lower graphics sales due to soft consumer demand.

SELECT AVG(sub.growth) AS avg_revenue_growth
FROM (
  SELECT
    am.ticker,
    MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2022 THEN am.value END) AS rev2022,
    MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2021 THEN am.value END) AS rev2021,
    CASE
      WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2021 THEN am.value END) IS NULL
           OR MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2021 THEN am.value END) = 0
      THEN NULL
      ELSE (MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2022 THEN am.value END) -
            MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2021 THEN am.value END))
           / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN am.period_end_year = 2021 THEN am.value END), 0)
    END AS growth
  FROM cn_4509b5c383744bb6.annual_metrics AS am
  WHERE am.metric = 'revenue'
    AND am.period_end_year IN (2021, 2022)
    AND am.unit = 'USD'
  GROUP BY am.ticker
) sub
WHERE sub.growth IS NOT NULL
LIMIT 1000

h17.answer_text:
Netflix’s revenue grew steadily from fiscal 2015 through fiscal 2022. In 2015 the company generated $6.78 billion, rising to $8.83 billion in 2016 (an increase of about $2.05 billion, ~30%). 2017 revenue reached $11.69 billion (+$2.86 billion, ~32%). 2018 saw $15.79 billion (+$4.10 billion, ~35%). 2019 grew to $20.16 billion (+$4.36 billion, ~28%). 2020 revenue was $24.99 billion (+$4.84 billion, ~24%). 2021 reached $29.70 billion (+$4.70 billion, ~19%). Finally, 2022 revenue was $31.62 billion (+$1.92 billion, ~6%).

The 2017 Form 10‑K outlines Netflix’s streaming strategy. It describes Netflix as a pioneer that launched its streaming service in 2007 and has built an ecosystem for internet‑connected screens. The core strategy is to grow the streaming membership business globally while meeting profit‑margin targets. Netflix aims to continuously improve the member experience by expanding streaming content with a programming mix that “delights our members,” enhancing the user interface, and extending the service to more internet‑connected devices. The company also emphasizes expanding original and exclusive programming and increasing international membership share.

h19.answer_text:
Microsoft’s total revenue grew from $91.2 billion in fiscal 2016 to $211.9 billion in fiscal 2023 – an increase of about $120.8 billion, or roughly a 132% rise, more than doubling the company’s top line over the seven‑year period.

The 2023 Form 10‑K highlights that the cloud business is a key growth engine. Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 22% to $111.6 billion, and Intelligent Cloud revenue grew 17% (with server products and cloud services up 19% and Azure‑related services up 29% on a consumption basis). The filing emphasizes three economies of scale in its cloud operations—lower unit costs from large datacenters, better utilization through aggregated demand, and multi‑tenancy that reduces maintenance labor. It also notes that Azure’s global‑scale platform offers hybrid consistency, AI capabilities, and strong security, positioning the cloud as central to Microsoft’s future growth strategy.

h23.answer_text:
Ulta Beauty’s net income rose steadily from fiscal 2019 to fiscal 2023. In 2019 the company reported net income of $658,559,000. By fiscal 2023 net income had increased to $1,242,408,000, an absolute rise of $583,849,000 (about an 88.7% increase over the four‑year period). 

The 2023 Form 10‑K describes Ulta’s loyalty program, Ultamate Rewards, as a “best‑in‑class” program that lets members earn points for every dollar spent on products and services, including purchases made with private‑label and co‑branded credit cards and at Ulta Beauty at Target. Points are valid for at least one year and can be redeemed for discounts on any product or service in stores or through digital channels. The company reports that more than 95% of total sales come from its roughly 40 million active members, and that loyalty members tend to spend more per visit than non‑members. Revenue from the program is deferred until points are redeemed or expire, with estimates of redemption rates based on historical patterns. The program also supports the company’s credit‑card offerings, which drive higher wallet share and provide additional customer insights.
